sources.quote: first published in a 1980 article by American philosopher John Searle
In 1980 John Searle published “Minds, Brains and Programs” in the journal The Behavioral and Brain Sciences

claims.text: hoan_canh: người không biết tiếng Trung trong phòng, làm theo sổ quy tắc thao tác ký hiệu, trả lời khiến người ngoài tin là người bản xứ

sources.quote: Imagine a native English speaker who knows no Chinese locked in a room full of boxes of Chinese symbols (a data base) together with a book of instructions for manipulating the symbols (the program).
he sends appropriate strings of Chinese characters back out under the door, and this leads those outside to mistakenly suppose there is a Chinese speaker in the room

claims.text: lua_chon b: Searle: cú pháp không phải ngữ nghĩa; thao tác ký hiệu mà không hiểu

sources.quote: Syntax is not by itself sufficient for, nor constitutive of, semantics.

claims.text: lua_chon a: Thuyết chức năng / AI mạnh

sources.quote: Strong AI is the view that suitably programmed computers (or the programs themselves) can understand natural language.

claims.text: phan_bien b: lập luận "hệ thống" và "robot"

sources.quote: The Systems Reply (which Searle says was originally associated with Yale, the home of Schank’s AI work) concedes that the man in the room does not understand Chinese.
The variant might be a computer embedded in a robotic body, having interaction with the physical world via sensors and motors (“The Robot Reply”)
